key_insight: A fully discrete mixed-dimensional model couples porous flow, viscoelastic deformation and frictional fracture contact, with proven discrete well-posedness, stability and a priori error estimates.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports reliable simulation of fractured porous materials where fluid flow, deformation and frictional contact interact.
method: Represent fractures as co-dimension-one interfaces with Darcy flow in both matrix and fractures.
Couple linear viscoelasticity to normal-compliance contact and Coulomb friction.
Discretize using conforming finite elements in space and implicit Euler time stepping.
evidence_signal: A numerical experiment computes errors and compares them with the theoretical estimates.
watch_item: The abstract reports a numerical error study, not experimental validation or demonstrated large-scale performance.
paper_title: Numerical analysis of coupled flow, deformation and frictional contact mechanics in a fractured porous medium
